top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a mature, clearly identified invention: magic-wavelength trapping lets many atoms be interrogated while motional and first-order light-shift perturbations are suppressed, and the resulting 10^-18 fractional uncertainty has been reproduced independently by several laboratories. The two-person allocation (Katori, Ye) and the citation scope (invention plus development to 10^-18) are defensible, with no attribution problem of the kind that afflicts large-collaboration proposals, so an award is preferable to no award.
